title: Set local systems: finite subobjects, colimits and finite etale total spaces
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. On its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], call a set sheaf a local system if it is ind-finite etale [def-per-ind-finite-etale-local-system]. A finite local system means a sheaf represented by a finite etale $X$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. (1) Every local system is the filtered union, in ambient set sheaves, of its finite local-system subsheaves. The full category of local systems is closed under all small ambient colimits and finite limits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. (2) Let $q:Y\to X$ be finite etale, with $Y$ Noetherian. The equivalence between set sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ and set sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ equipped with a map to $h_Y$ sends $E$ to its total-space sheaf $q_!E\to h_Y$. In the reverse direction it sends $p:F\to h_Y$ to the sheaf whose sections on $(a:U\to Y)$ are $\{t\in F(U):p(t)=a\}$. It preserves the corresponding group actions, with a $G$-action over $h_Y$ corresponding to a $q^{-1}G$-action on $E$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Pullback $q^{-1}$ preserves local systems, and $q_!$ sends local systems on $Y$ to local systems on $X$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Propositions 7.2.2–7.2.4, pp. 301–302; the finite-subobject union and the slice/total-space equivalence q_! are used explicitly in the proof of Lemma 7.2.6, p. 302. No torsion extension-closure assertion is included.
